name: Tanqueray London Dry Gin
production: Botanicals added during the second distillation
Recipe a trade secret (four known botanicals)
Surviving 'Old Tom' still moved to Cameronbridge (Wikipedia, citation needed)
history: 1830 | First distilled by Charles Tanqueray in Bloomsbury, London
1838 | Edward & Charles Tanqueray & Co established on Vine Street, London
1868 | Charles Tanqueray died; son Charles Waugh Tanqueray inherited
1898 | Merged with Gordon's to form Tanqueray Gordon & Co (Gordon's Wikipedia)
1940s | London distillery severely damaged in WWII air raids; production later moved to Cameronbridge
2023 | UK strength reduced from 43.1% to 41.3%; 'Export Strength' label dropped
finish: Juniper and a hint of pepper/spice
expressions: Tanqueray No. TEN | 2000, 47.3%, whole grapefruit, orange, lime, chamomile
Tanqueray Rangpur | 2006, 41.3%, Rangpur lime, ginger, bay leaf
notes: Gin Guide suggests G&T with lime garnish (not official). Gin Guide says 43.1% domestic, 47.3% export. No official Tanqueray page fetched.
